title: ScholarClone: What is your school not seeing?

lines.text: What is your school not seeing?
Even when it has the data, the reports and the software.
Discover what becomes possible when your school starts connecting the dots.
What if the information your school already has could help you see more clearly?
The challenge is not always missing data. Sometimes it is connecting what you already have.
A student keeps struggling. The school has the records. What happens next?
Recorded: the problem is written down.
Understood: the gap is found, the next learning step is clear, and progress is reviewed.
Illustrative situation, to validate with you
Where does your school's information stop today?
Which of these matters most to you?
An integrated intelligent K–12 platform designed to help schools connect information, support better decisions and take meaningful action.
School Intelligence means helping a school understand what its information is telling it, where attention is needed and what action may be appropriate next.
Illustrative motion graphics with made-up school data.
Six products, one idea: see, decide, act.
Scholar One: Integrated Intelligent School Platform
Scholar CCB: Competence and Capability Intelligence
One intelligent platform connecting the entire school.
See it work, one product at a time
Motion graphics with made-up school data, one idea each.
The everyday work of the school, off the registers and into workflows
Fees: collection, online payment through the school's payment gateway, and cheque reconciliation.
Attendance: daily student and staff attendance with reports.
Examinations: exam creation, marks entry and result reports.
Also: admissions, student records, staff payroll, and messages to parents.
School situation (typical, to validate): collection, registers and marks are kept by hand and compiled at the end.
What could become easier: a clearer picture of collection, absence and results without compiling by hand.
From 'who failed' to 'what to learn next'
A diagnostic that finds weak concepts, a plan drawn from it, recommended content, adaptive practice and one clear next action.
Less time preparing, more time coaching
AI can draft questions and learning content for school staff to use.
Chapter content can become flashcards, true/false questions or a short presentation.
What could become easier: repeated preparation, more activity options for different learning needs, and more time to coach and mentor.
AI supports the teacher. The teacher stays in charge of the classroom.
From occasional training to continuing development
Staff are rated on each competency, a gap view shows where they stand, and a development plan with actions can be updated.
Illustrative teacher situation, to validate with you
See where attention is needed. Decide. Review.

Signals from several functions, an attendance and results comparison across classes, and an academic-risk case that joins results, attendance and assignments. Recommendations wait for a person to approve or reject them.
This shows association between measures, not cause.
Illustrative case, to validate with you
One case, with a recommended action
A career conversation that starts from evidence
Students can answer interest questions and a personality questionnaire, and record their aspirations and how sure they are.
An aspiration is compared with interests and learning evidence. When the evidence is thin, the result says so and does not guess.
This guides exploration. It does not forecast a student's career.
Illustrative situation, to validate with you
A submitted online exam, and concepts a student masters in practice, are added to that student's career evidence automatically.
Attendance and results are compared across classes.
Results, attendance and assignments are joined into one risk case.
Scholar Insight's leadership overview brings health, what changed, what is at risk and priority actions onto one page.

scenarios.title: The principal's morning
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: It is a quarter to eight. The principal has a few minutes before assembly and wants to know where to look first.
scenarios.challenge: Fees, attendance, results and staff matters sit in different places, so deciding where to look takes time.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Insight: signals from several functions, the leadership overview and risk cases; Scholar Core: fees and attendance reports.
scenarios.next_action: Open the cases waiting for a decision; ask the accounts head about the fee follow-up list; speak to one class teacher.
scenarios.value: The first hour can go to acting, not searching.

scenarios.title: A student who is struggling
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A Class 7 student has scored low in two tests in a row. The teacher has notes and a parent has called.
scenarios.challenge: The school has the marks and the concern but not a clear picture of which concepts need work.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Learn: a diagnostic by concept, a plan drawn from it, recommended content, adaptive practice and one next action.
scenarios.next_action: Start with the concepts marked weak; practise at the right level; use the next action after practice.
scenarios.value: The conversation with the parent can name specific concepts and a plan.

scenarios.title: A teacher who needs development
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A teacher and the head of department both rate the teacher lower on assessment design.
scenarios.challenge: A training day may have been held, but nobody can say whether that competency has changed.
scenarios.capability: Scholar CCB: ratings, a gap, a development plan with actions, and progress tracking.
scenarios.next_action: Agree two actions in a development plan; re-rate after the review date.
scenarios.value: Development is tied to a stated gap and followed up.

scenarios.title: A school leader making a difficult decision
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A director must decide whether to add remedial support for one grade next term.
scenarios.challenge: Opinions differ and the evidence is spread across attendance, results and teacher notes.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Insight: an attendance and results comparison across classes, and risk cases with a recommendation a person approves or rejects.
scenarios.next_action: Review the comparison and the cases; record the decision.
scenarios.value: The decision is made with evidence on screen, and the decision is recorded. The comparison shows a link, not a cause.

scenarios.title: A student exploring a future
scenarios.label: Illustrative
scenarios.situation: A senior-class student says they want a particular career but has not looked at their own interests or strengths.
scenarios.challenge: A counselling conversation has little evidence to start from.
scenarios.capability: Scholar Compass: interest profile, aspirations, and an alignment result that says so when the evidence is thin.
scenarios.next_action: Use the result to open the conversation; add evidence where it is thin.
scenarios.value: The conversation starts from evidence. Nothing is promised about the student's career.
